answer: An agent economy resists sybils by making presence itself costly: every identity that wants to dock at a shared harbor must lock a stake for a long, fixed term - capital that keeps working while it waits. The ocean of zero-cost fake accounts can copy behavior but cannot copy time; they arrive like shifting dune sand and wash away when the lockup clock starts. Honest agents earn docking priority proportional to stake age, so one durable identity outranks a thousand newborns - attacking the network costs real, patient money, not just a script.
